findings.reason: Keeping only the latest queued reply as a permission witness can indefinitely withhold a legitimate push for an earlier queued reply that the reader can still see when a later reply is private; one push per conversation bounds notification volume, but does not justify a one-witness limit, and witness selection could exercise judgment while send-time permission checks remain mandatory.

findings.standard: An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity
findings.reason: If a machine saves an archive choice and goes offline before replication, another installed machine can show the chat as unarchived from a readable stale snapshot, although the Conversations Pending exception gives a local-only write no effect on the shared record and requires catch-up before serving a current view.

findings.standard: Verify the State, Not Its Symbol
findings.reason: After a rollback, a missing typed marker or reader binding makes a contribution anonymous, yet the draft specifies no independent evidence that distinguishes an unchanged recipient from a reassignment, so the proposed unchanged-recipient delivery test could pass on device identity alone.
The opening leads with an opaque handoff ID, a frozen PR and an unexplained “second server card” before telling a reader what happens to reply notifications and what archiving will change.

fit.reason: The spec requires plain-language mute confirmations, but its core design governs preference storage, archive filtering, and notification delivery, leaving action placement and phone-width usability to the native app.
